Subject: Arcadia MSA - redlines and two quick open points

Laura — attaching our redline to the MSA and the updated order form (note: redlines embedded). Two items we want to call out explicitly so they don't get lost in the track changes: 

1) Governing law — Arcadia strongly prefers California law (our HQ is there). If you must insist on Delaware, we need a reciprocal concession elsewhere.

2) Equitable relief / injunctive carve — we want injunctive relief for data protection/IP preserved in court (not forced into arbitration). Our standard language keeps injunctive remedies out of arbitration for breach of confidentiality and IP, and we cannot accept a blanket waiver.

Can your team propose specific carve language that preserves our right to immediate injunctive relief while still keeping most disputes in arbitration? Also confirm who your signatory will be for the order form so procurement can loop internal approvers.

Attachments: Arcadia_MSA_redline_20280715.docx (MS Word redline), OrderForm_v2.pdf

Thanks,
Samantha Lee

Date: 2028-07-16T10:03:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Arcadia MSA - redlines and two quick open points

Samantha — thanks for the redline and the clear callouts. We ran the points by our legal and sales teams; suggested compromise below to keep momentum and limit tail risk. Happy to jump on a quick 20-min call if you prefer to talk through.

Summary of Redwood proposal (high level):
- Governing law: Delaware law for the Agreement; however, we will accept California venue for enforcement of injunctive relief related to Arcadia's customer data or Arcadia-owned IP, limited to courts in California.
- Dispute resolution: Binding arbitration (AAA/ICDR) for all other claims limited by the MSA, seat of arbitration: New York, neutral rules.
- Injunctive relief carve: Routine carve preserving parties' right to seek interim injunctive or other equitable relief in court (i.e., \"Notwithstanding the agreement to arbitrate, either party may seek temporary injunctive relief in a court of competent jurisdiction to protect its intellectual property rights or prevent unauthorized disclosure of Customer Data.\")
- Mutuality: Redwood requests the carve be mutual and limited to narrow categories (IP, confidentiality, data protection).

We think this gets both parties what they need: Delaware law for predictability, streamlined arbitration for commercial disputes, and a narrow, reciprocal court carve for urgent injunctive relief. We can provide redline language if this is acceptable in principle.

Cc'ing David and Karthik for final legal redline and playbook on signatory/PO path.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2028-07-18T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Arcadia MSA - redlines and two quick open points

Laura — draft language below (legal has approved the narrow carve). Please push this back to Arcadia as our formal redline. I left the statutory references intentionally light to avoid a fight over venue-specific phrasing.

--- Proposed redline (insert into Section X: Dispute Resolution / Injunctive Relief) ---
Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the Parties agree that any dispute shall be submitted to binding arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association (or its successor) under the Commercial Arbitration Rules. The seat of arbitration shall be New York, New York, and the arbitrator(s) shall apply the substantive law selected in this Agreement.

Notwithstanding the foregoing agreement to arbitrate, either Party may seek interim or provisional injunctive or other equitable relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to protect its proprietary rights, to prevent or limit the unauthorized disclosure of Confidential Information or Customer Data, or to preserve evidence, and each Party irrevocably submits to personal jurisdiction in the courts of California for such purposes when the seeking party is asserting rights related to Customer Data or asserted IP rights associated with Arcadia's operations. Such limited right to seek provisional relief in court shall not be deemed a waiver of the agreement to arbitrate disputes set forth above.

--- end redline ---

Two operational notes: 
- If Arcadia insists on California law as governing law, we can swap governing law to California but retain New York as the arbitration seat; that's less ideal for Redwood but worth having as a last-resort concession.
- For procurement: Karthik, please confirm whether Redwood can sign the order form (electronic signatory) or whether we need VP-level signature for this deal size.

-David
David Kim
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks David — language looks good to me. A couple quick commercial points from procurement/sales ops: 
- We should avoid adding an entire new venue appendix; keep carve inline to reduce negotiation friction.
- For the mutuality clause, confirm that "Customer Data" is defined in a manner that covers PHI/security-sensitive subsets since Arcadia handles patient data (we should not broaden inadvertently).
- I'll confirm signatory: Redwood can use delegated signatory for Order Form up to $500k ARR; above that we need VP approval. Current OCF indicates first-year ARR estimate ~$420k, so delegated signatory is fine.

I'll reply to Samantha now with the formal redline and the signatory confirmation.

Thanks — Karthik
